findings.where: Destinations section heading "Where we're starting" at desktop (it fills the bottom of the first screen at about 130 px type), and at phone width, where it is still set larger than the hero's MantaHostels h1
findings.fault: The hierarchy is upside down. A secondary section heading is two to three times the size of the hero's main heading, so it is what the eye lands on first. At desktop its two huge lines take up the rest of the first screen, which pushes the three destination cards, the page's second job, below the fold behind a heading.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker who comes to plan their next stop. Their eye goes to a label instead of to what the site is or which places it covers, and at desktop they have to scroll past a wall of heading before they see a destination.

findings.where: Hero at desktop: the text column (claim, h1, body, both buttons) against the nav wordmark, the destinations heading and the card row
findings.fault: The hero's content starts about 230 px further right (x≈424) than the left edge shared by the nav wordmark, the section below and the cards (x≈195), and it doesn't fill or centre the space. So the page has two unrelated left edges (continuity breaks), and the hero's right half is empty teal while the mascot sits alone in the far corner of the wave, cut off from the content it belongs with.
findings.who_objects: A first-time desktop visitor. The ragged edges and the stray mascot make a pre-launch page look unfinished, which matters when it is asking for their email on trust.

findings.where: Hero, the stack of eyebrow claim and h1
findings.fault: The brand name repeats the nav wordmark just above it and gets the hero's big type. The line that says what the product does ("The better way to find hostels in Indonesia.") is set small as an eyebrow above it. When you squint, the hero says "MantaHostels" twice and the offer barely registers.
findings.who_objects: A traveller scanning on a phone mid-trip. They need to know in a glance that this is a hostel finder for Indonesia, and the loudest thing on screen only tells them a name they have already seen in the nav.

findings.where: Hero action pair: the coral email button above the outline "Explore destinations" button, at desktop and at phone width
findings.fault: The two actions are shaped as if they came from different systems. One is a full pill and the other a square-cornered box, they are different widths, and they are stacked loosely, so they don't read as a matched primary and secondary pair (similarity). At phone width the coral button wraps the email address onto two lines and becomes a large blob next to a short one-line box.
findings.who_objects: A visitor deciding what to do next. The mismatched pair looks unfinished, and on a phone the two-line coral block reads as a paragraph rather than a button.
